scope: Price-blind factual update only; distinguishes public claims/reporting from demonstrated state authority.

identity.question: Will Reza Pahlavi lead Iran in 2026?

rule: YES only if Pahlavi de facto exercises primary Iranian state governing authority by Dec 31, including effective control of armed forces, national institutions, and core executive decisions; symbolic/exile/foreign recognition or nomination alone do not qualify.

observations.dated_content: Site lists Oct 2, 2026 as his latest statement at capture; describes a proposed transition from the Islamic Republic and lists “maximum defections” and “maximum organization” as strategy pillars. Page does not report appointment to Iranian office or exercise of domestic governing authority.

observations.reported: Parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi as defense and armed-forces-logistics minister; IRNA reports 237 votes for and 15 against, 277 members present. President Masoud Pezeshkian nominated him Oct 5. He succeeded acting minister Majid Ibn al-Reza, who had served since Feb 28.

Corroborates Oct 18 minister appointment; says parliament had convened online since the Feb 28 war began, and reports the minister-designate consulted senior military officials including IRGC commander-in-chief Ahmad Vahidi. This is reporting on institutions/contacts, not direct proof of nationwide command effectiveness.

bounded_assessment: These observations show an exile transition platform and ongoing Iranian presidential/parliamentary/defense appointments as reported by state media and an independent outlet. They do not establish a transition or Pahlavi control of armed forces, ministries, capital, or executive decisions. No specific current security fracture or verified domestic defections are established by these three sources; bounded scope is not an absence finding.
